title: Cohomology of a module in degree zero
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $M\in D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ and let $\mathcal{N}$ be an
invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module with
$M\cong\mathcal{N}[0]$. Then $H^i(M)=0$ for $i\neq0$ and $H^0(M)\cong\mathcal{N}$. If
$M\cong E[-i]$ with $E$ locally free of rank $r$ (cf. [def-pc-finite-locally-free] and its [lem-pc-flf-properties]),
then $H^j(M)=0$ for $j\neq i$ and $H^i(M)\cong E$.

proof.text: An isomorphism in the derived category is represented by a zig-zag of quasi-isomorphisms, and each quasi-isomorphism induces isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves. Therefore the cohomology of $M$ may be computed from either displayed representative.

The complex $\mathcal{N}[0]$ has $\mathcal{N}$ in degree $0$ and the zero object in every other degree, so its degree-$0$ cohomology is $\mathcal{N}$ and its cohomology in every degree $i\ne0$ is zero. Thus $H^0(M)\cong\mathcal{N}$ and $H^i(M)=0$ for $i\ne0$.

The shift $E[-i]$ is the complex with $E$ in degree $i$ and the zero object in every other degree. Its degree-$i$ cohomology is therefore $E$, while all other cohomology objects vanish. Using the first step for the isomorphism $M\cong E[-i]$ gives $H^i(M)\cong E$ and $H^j(M)=0$ for $j\ne i$.
